display.purpose: Page titles and hero headlines. The editorial signal — tight negative letter-spacing carries the system's voice.

headline.purpose: Card titles and section heads inside dense screens.

title.purpose: List-item titles, primary inline labels, table primary cells.

body.purpose: Paragraph prose, secondary content. Capped at 65–75ch.

label.purpose: Section captions, group headers, form labels, table column heads, stat-tile labels. The wide tracking is the rhythm.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Quiet boundary where two surfaces meet. The structural grid weight.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Default paper-card shadow at rest. Grounded — reads as paper resting on paper.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Popovers, dropdowns, larger surfaces that benefit from definition. The lift moment.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: Focus halo on primary actions hover. Pressed Sage at 8%.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Above-anchored shadow on the BottomSheet primitive.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard-focus halo with 1px paper gap so the ring reads against any tinted surface.

motion.name: editorial-ease
motion.purpose: Default ease-out for state transitions across the system. No bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: fade-up
motion.purpose: Entrance for list rows and stat tiles. 8px translateY origin.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.purpose: Entrance for popovers, dropdowns, the active stat tile lift.

motion.name: bottom-sheet-spring
motion.purpose: BottomSheet open and drag-snap motion. Replaced with instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview: JobFlex's interface is a workshop that has been kept. Organized, a little beautiful, ready for the next job. Type and whitespace carry the weight; the green appears like a marked-up margin note. The system serves three scenes at once: a contractor in direct sunlight on a jobsite, a contractor at a desk at 9pm finishing invoices, and a contractor standing next to a homeowner presenting an estimate. The voice is composed, accurate, trustworthy. Editorial restraint over template-cream. Numeric-honest: money, dates, durations line up in tabular columns. Single-typeface: Geist does the entire hierarchy. The accent (Pressed Sage) is the system's confidence signal used decisively on primary actions, active nav, accepted state, and key numerals, not sprinkled as decoration. This is a deliberate counter-positioning against the four traps that 'contractor software' snaps to: hi-vis construction cliché, generic SaaS-cream, AI-startup purple-gradient, and consumer-cute.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-paper background, cool near-black ink, Pressed Sage as the single accent.
Layered depth: grounded low-chroma shadows + surface tonal layering. Hairlines are a quiet secondary tool.
Geist as the single typeface; weight, scale, and letter-spacing carry hierarchy.
Editorial table treatment: hairline dividers, whisper-zebra, comfortable row height, tabular numerals on money/views/dates.
Status pills get subtle tonal fills per state; never gray-on-gray.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Pressed Sage is the only accent. It is the system's signal that something is primary, accepted, or moves money. Used confidently on primary CTAs and key states; never sprinkled decoratively. Calibrated at ≤10% of any screen — its rarity preserves the signal.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is tinted toward the brand hue subtly cool, never pure gray. #000 and #fff are prohibited as surface or text colors.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Emerald, Rose, and Amber appear only when they encode state. Pressed Sage is brand; the supporting trio is state.

rules.name: The Tonal-Pill Rule
rules.body: Status pills carry per-state tonal pairs. Never gray-on-gray for differentiated states.

rules.name: The Single-Typeface Rule
rules.body: Geist does the entire hierarchy. Do not introduce a serif, script, or second sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeric Rule
rules.body: Money, counts, dates, durations, percentages use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Mixed proportional and tabular in the same column is forbidden.

rules.name: The Quiet-Caps Rule
rules.body: The quiet-caps utility (11px, 500, +0.14em, uppercase) is the system's section caption. Do not bump its size to make it more important.

rules.name: The Layered-Depth Rule
rules.body: Static surfaces get depth from tonal layering and the Card shadow at rest. Pop and Sheet Lift are reserved for elements that temporarily float.

rules.name: The Hairline-Beats-Border Rule
rules.body: Default to 0.5px hairlines. Use full 1px borders only when an element must remain legible on top of a colored surface.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Card Rule
rules.body: Cards are not the default container. Use .paper-card only when the contained content is logically a discrete object.

rules.name: The Hairline-Is-The-Boundary Rule
rules.body: The 0.5px hairline is how the system signals structure where shadows don't carry the load.

rules.name: The Confident-Accent Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons, active sidebar items, Accepted/Paid pills, and key stat numerals all bind to --accent. The accent is the system's identity signal, not a sparkle.

dos: Do use Pressed Sage (#1f7a52) confidently on primary CTAs, active nav, Accepted/Paid pills, key numerals, and focus rings.
Do prefer hairline 0.5px borders over full 1px borders for static dividers.
Do use quiet-caps (11px, 500, +0.14em tracking, uppercase, --ink-soft) for every section caption, group label, form label, and table column header.
Do use tabular numerals on money, dates, durations, counts, percentages.
Do treat depth as layered: grounded shadows for cards at rest, tonal surface stacking, Pop only when something temporarily floats.
Do tint every neutral toward cool.
Do keep body line length to 65–75ch.
Do apply per-state tonal fills to status pills.
Do ensure all mobile touch targets are ≥44px and contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
donts: Don't use construction-cliché visuals: no hi-vis safety yellow, no hardhat icons, no hammer mascots, no blueprint backgrounds, no jobsite-photo heroes, no orange CTAs.
Don't drift toward generic SaaS-cream: no HubSpot blue, no identical card grids, no hero-metric template tiles.
Don't use AI-startup purple-gradients, sparkle icons on AI features, glassmorphism as default, or Linear-clone dark.
Don't use mascot illustrations, playful pastels, gamified streaks, or oversized emoji icons.
Don't use #000 or #fff as surface or text colors.
Don't introduce a second typeface. Geist is the entire system.
Don't use side-stripe borders greater than 1px as a colored accent. The Sidebar active rail is the one calibrated exception.
Don't reach for a modal as the first thought.
Don't invent a new accent color.
Don't add md: / lg: / xl: Tailwind responsive variants in new mobile work.
Don't add dark-mode (.dark) variants in new work.
Don't introduce a token that doesn't already exist in globals.css or tailwind.config.ts.
